title: Sealed tokens from the pairing rendezvous
about: What GET /v1/pair/{pid} returns as sealedToken once the owner has approved, recorded from the real relay. The phone opens it with the X25519 secret it made for the pairing; nothing else opens it. See README.md in this folder for the format and for what a Rust reader calls.

format.box: libsodium crypto_box_seal: an anonymous sealed box (X25519, XSalsa20-Poly1305)
format.encoding: base64url without padding (canonical: unused low bits zero)
format.layout: ephemeralPublic (32 bytes) || tag (16 bytes) || ciphertext (the same length as the plaintext)
format.nonce: BLAKE2b with a 24 byte output over ephemeralPublic || recipientPublic
format.key: crypto_box_beforenm: HSalsa20 over the X25519 shared secret of the recipient secret and ephemeralPublic
format.plaintext: the ASCII device token: "oaiyrt1." + 11 characters + "." + 43 characters, 63 bytes. It is never written in this file: plaintextSha256 is the check.
format.refuse: a box that does not authenticate, a length under 48 bytes, or an X25519 shared secret of all zeros (a small-order ephemeral key), even when the box authenticates under the key that shared secret gives (refused[8] and refused[9])

recipient.note: The test phone of Appendix A3: a fixed public test key, never a real one.
